text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on streaming route /v1/stream for model redwood-llama-13b-int8-calib-v2. Current p95=1.1s p99=5.8s (baseline p99 ~1.2s). Error rate stable. Affected region: us-west1.
emma_oncall: Ack. I’m oncall. Paging SRE.
raj_sre: On it, joining. Seeing large tail; traces show many requests stuck in 'kv_dequant' step.
liz_dev: Noted — that model was part of the int8 calibration rollout started 18:02 UTC. Can we confirm rollout scope?
noah_ops: Rollout config: 40% traffic to int8-calib-v2 for streaming-routes, warm pool enabled. Canary looked fine earlier at low QPS.
emma_oncall: Customer-facing impact? Any 5xx or stream disconnects?
support-bot: Customer impact flags: 3 customers with degraded tail latency (requests slow but success). Top impacted: search-saas-prod, chat-x. No automated retries triggered.
raj_sre: Captured traces: many TTLs show long wait inside dequant kernel (CUDA stall). Example trace snippet: `dequant_kernel -> kvcache_lookup -> dequant_kernel (hang)`.
liz_dev: That matches a calibration fallback path we added — under certain KV cache sizes the int8 dequant path does extra reconciliation loops. Might be an edge-case.
alice_pm: Anything customer-facing we should announce?
emma_oncall: Hold public comms until we have mitigation. Priority: reduce p99, restore SLOs.
raj_sre: Quick mitigations to test: 1) route streaming traffic for this model to fp16 stable variant 2) disable int8-calib rollout flag 3) drain and cold-start warm pool nodes (expensive). Will try 1 and 2 first.
noah_ops: I can flip routing in ~2m via traffic-router. Command: `traffic-router promote --from redwood-llama-13b-int8-calib-v2 --to redwood-llama-13b-fp16-stable --percent 40 --route streaming`
emma_oncall: Please do 1) now and monitor p99.
noah_ops: Executing: `traffic-router promote ...` (running)
incident-bot: Deploy-bot: traffic-router change submitted by noah_ops at 18:39:12 UTC — change id cr-8921.
noah_ops: Change applied. Rolling 40% off int8-calib-v2 -> fp16-stable for streaming.
raj_sre: Monitoring. Live metrics: p99 dropping from 5.8s -> 2.0s within a minute. Still above baseline but much better.
liz_dev: Good. Meanwhile I'm preparing an immediate rollback of int8-calib-v2 (calibration artifact) from the model catalog so it stops receiving new deployments. Command: `catalog rollback redwood-llama-13b-int8-calib-v2 --reason "tail latency regression"`
emma_oncall: Assign action owners: raj to monitor, liz to coordinate rollback and fix, noah to keep routing changes, alice to draft internal blurb.
alice_pm: Drafting internal note. Will include customer list and ETA for follow-up.
raj_sre: p99 now 1.4s after 5m, p95 stable at 0.9s. Looks within SLO window for most customers. Continuing to watch.
noah_ops: I also flipped the feature-flag that enables the additional reconciliation loop: `ff-toggle disable int8-calib-reconcile-v2` as a precaution on canary nodes.
liz_dev: Thanks. That flag was meant to be benign but apparently interacts with kv cache fragmentation. I'll open a ticket with repro steps and add to hotfix branch.
support-bot: Auto-note: impacted customer tickets created for search-saas-prod and chat-x. Severity: medium (latency-only).
emma_oncall: Are we sure there are no lingering stream stalls? Any client disconnects?
raj_sre: No disconnects observed. Streaming chunk delays were longer but clients eventually receive. Also confirmed no 5xx spikes.
liz_dev: Quick diff: earlier change added a fallback dequantization step that reprocesses KV ranges when mismatch detected. Under high streaming concurrency and certain KV cache growth patterns it can re-enqueue the same request, causing tail amplification. I'll back out that fallback until we have a safe guard.
alice_pm: For customer comms: ETA for rollback/fix?
liz_dev: I can push a hotfix to disable fallback in ~90m, but traffic routing fallback to fp16 already bought us time. Prefer final fix after a proper repro.
emma_oncall: OK. Short-term: keep routing to fp16 for streaming for 24h and disable int8-calib rollout. Long-term: postmortem with root cause and blocking test.
raj_sre: Logging an incident ticket: INC-2026-042 — quant-calib-stream-tail. Adding logs, traces, and timeline.
noah_ops: I've queued a low-priority cold restart of 2 warm pool machines on schedule to avoid further fragmentation; will be non-disruptive due to traffic routing.
emma_oncall: Any customer escalation required?
support-bot: No customers requested immediate escalation; two customers reported higher latency but accept follow-up.
alice_pm: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups in 2 hrs with status and ETA for permanent fix.
liz_dev: Creating PR reference: GH#rwd/serving#7321. Will link repro artifacts.
raj_sre: Monitoring window 30m. Will update thread on any regressions. If p99 creeps >2s we re-open paging.
incident-bot: Note: SLO breach window closed at 18:49:40 UTC (p99 within thresholds). Incident state: mitigated but investigating.
emma_oncall: Thanks all. After 30m handoff: if stable, move to post-incident review doc and assign owners for fix and tests.
alice_pm: Assigned owners in tracker: liz_dev -> fix, raj_sre -> verification & alert tuning, noah_ops -> routing failover playbook.
noah_ops: Adding a one-click rollback button to console for precision-rollouts this week.
liz_dev: I'll add a replay test for streaming kv cache patterns to our CI so calibration runs under heavier concurrency.
raj_sre: Quick follow-up: add an alert for dequant kernel duration >1s to catch earlier.
emma_oncall: Closing on-call here; I'll file the postmortem and schedule a 1-hr RCA tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
